fields.name: DataConnectionManager execution operations (internal)
fields.contract: Per this component's own committed responsibility (components/resilient-command-execution): DataConnectionManager is an internal class, not a public API surface, and every public data method in the library (on DatabasesBase, ShardDataConnection and related facades) delegates to one instance of it, one instance per read or write endpoint. Its sole public member is the read-only ConnectionString property, which resolves the endpoint's connection string via the endpoint's IDataConnection configuration. Six of its seven execution members take a Query, a DbParameterCollection and a shardParameterOrdinal and form one family varying only in the shape of the materialized result: ReturnAsync<TValue1,TValue2,TValue3> reads up to three named output-parameter-or-column values as a tuple; ReturnAsync(Query,...) reads the command's integer return-value parameter, adding it to the command if the caller did not supply one; ListAsync<TModel> maps every result-set row to a List<TModel>; ListAsync<TValue1,TValue2,TValue3> reads up to three named column values per row into a List of tuples; QueryAsync<TArg,TModel> hands the open reader, the command's parameters and an optional caller-supplied argument to a caller-supplied QueryResultModelHandler<TArg,TModel> and returns its result; RunAsync executes the command for its side effects only and returns nothing. The seventh member, RunBatchAsync<TResult>, does not fit that family: it takes no Query, DbParameterCollection or shardParameterOrdinal at all, only a caller-supplied BatchBase<TResult>; it runs that batch against one connection inside one transaction and returns its result, committing the transaction only if the batch completes without throwing, and it binds no shard id to a command parameter, though it does hand the endpoint's own shard id to the batch's ExecuteAsync (DataConnectionManager.cs line 578). When the caller-supplied ordinal identifies a parameter, each of the six Query-driven members binds the endpoint's shard id to that parameter in the command it builds, by adding it to the per-execution parameter values that the provider applies over the copied parameters (a caller-supplied per-execution value for that parameter, such as a ShardsValues entry, takes precedence). None of them writes the shard id, or anything else, into the caller's DbParameterCollection, so one collection can be shared by concurrently executing shards of a ShardSet fan-out. Every member except the two tuple-returning ReturnAsync/ListAsync overloads first checks a caller-supplied mock-results dictionary and, on a match, returns the stored value directly, without opening a connection, running the resilience policy, or touching the circuit breaker's failure count. ReturnAsync(Query,...), ListAsync<TModel>, QueryAsync<TArg,TModel> and RunAsync key that lookup by query.Name, so distinct queries can be mocked independently; RunBatchAsync<TResult> has no Query object and instead keys its lookup by the fixed sentinel key string.Empty, so at most one mocked batch result can ever be registered in a given mock-results dictionary, regardless of which BatchBase<TResult> is run. The two tuple-returning overloads accept no mock-results parameter and so can never be mocked. Every non-mocked execution path of the six Query-driven members opens a fresh provider connection and command on every attempt and executes under the endpoint's own resilience policy, passing the cancellation token the policy hands it to both the connection open and the command execution (including RunAsync's non-query execution), so cancellation requested while a command runs is observed by the provider. RunBatchAsync<TResult>'s non-mocked path likewise executes under that same resilience policy, but ExecuteBatchAsync only opens a connection and begins a transaction itself; it delegates the actual command construction to the caller-supplied batch's own ExecuteAsync method, which receives that open connection and transaction directly.
